propositions: a rejected tickets-branch auto-push succeeds locally and reports success to the caller while the push is actually rejected by remote policy, remaining invisible for hours until discovered by manual git push
the rejection reason (GH013, hook declined, etc.) is captured by the git subprocess but discarded before reaching the caller, so only a generic retries-exhausted message is logged

terminal policy rejections (push protection, branch protection, hook decline) are misclassified as retriable non-fast-forward failures due to an over-broad substring match on 'rejected', causing futile fetch+merge retry cycles instead of immediate failure reporting
ticket event payloads in comments are never scanned for secrets on write, allowing live credentials to be committed and pushed before being discovered by code-review gating

the PUSH_PENDING backlog signal is computed only at pull-time in fsck and never re-announced on subsequent writes, so an eight-hour accumulation of 122 unpushed commits produces identical one-line warnings and remains undetected without explicit fsck
on async push policy the warning is spawned as a detached process with stderr redirected to /dev/null, making rejection completely undeliverable to the writing caller
